_comment: Plain-language WC3 jargon for the learner-card tooltips (homepage; later the in-viewer build-order panel). Loaded by client/js/Glossary.js. `term` = the tooltip header (keep short), `def` = 1-2 sentences, `match` = every word / abbreviation / variant that should trigger the tooltip (case-insensitive, whole-word). Multi-word phrases win over their sub-words. Plain ASCII only.

terms.def: Your tech level, set by upgrading your main hall. T1 is the start; T2 and T3 unlock stronger units, buildings, and upgrades. "Teching" means paying for that upgrade.
Neutral monsters that guard spots, gold mines, and items around the map. "Creeping" is hunting them for gold, items, and hero experience.
A fixed group of creeps guarding a location or item drop. Camps are colour-coded by difficulty: green easy, orange medium, red hard.
A second town hall on another gold mine, for extra income. Greedy, but pays off if it survives long enough.
Hurting the enemy's economy or hero -- killing workers, poking with a hero -- without committing to a full fight.
Spending resources to reach a higher tier or unlock advanced units/upgrades, rather than on more current-tier army.
Controlling individual units mid-fight: kiting, focusing one target, pulling wounded units back, dodging spells.
The economic side: keep making workers, keep production running, raise supply in time, and don't let gold/lumber pile up unused.
Heroes level up by being near things that die (yours or the enemy's). Higher level = more stats and an extra ability point.
The wood resource, harvested from trees by your workers. Needed for most buildings, upgrades, and casters.
Your population cap. Every unit costs food; build farms / burrows / ziggurats / moon wells to raise it. 90 from buildings, 100 hard cap.
Warcraft III's anti-snowball tax: above 50 food you mine less gold per trip, and above 80 even less. Big armies cost more to sustain.
Stuck not making units because you've hit the food cap. Build supply ahead of need so this never happens.
Gold or lumber sitting unspent in the bank. It does nothing there -- spend it on workers, army, buildings, or upgrades.
Attack, step back, attack again -- so ranged units keep hitting a melee chaser without ever getting hit. Hit-and-run.
Concentrating your army's attacks on one enemy unit at a time so it dies fast, instead of spreading damage around.
Attacking at the moment you have an edge -- a finished upgrade, a hero level, a unit count -- before the opponent catches up.
Holding vision and presence over the map -- key creep camps, expansion spots, watch towers -- so you know where the enemy is and what they're doing.
Sending a unit (or owl / sentinel / flying machine) to see the enemy's build and army so you can react instead of guessing.
An attack-move command: units advance and auto-attack anything they meet. Convenient -- but it walks fragile ranged units into melee, so don't a-move them.
Damage or spells that hit everything in an area -- Blizzard, Death and Decay, Mortar shots, Frost Nova. Clumped armies get melted by it; spread out.
Spellcasting support units -- Priest, Sorceress, Shaman, Witch Doctor, Necromancer, Banshee, Dryad, Druids. Powerful but fragile; protect them and watch their mana.
Temporary units conjured by a spell -- Water Elemental, Treants, Feral Spirits, Skeletons, Serpent Wards. Cheap or free and expendable; re-summon when they expire.
A permanent improvement bought at a building -- attack/armor levels, caster training, ability unlocks. +1 attack across a whole army is huge; don't skip these.
The planned sequence of buildings, workers, and units in the opening -- what you make, and in what order, before the game gets reactive.
How you start: which hero you make first, and which first buildings and units. It sets the tone for the rest of the game.
Committing everything to one attack with no fallback. It wins the game if it lands and loses it if it doesn't.
Both players ignoring each other's armies and attacking each other's bases at the same time -- usually decided by who kills the other's base or production first.
Human ability that turns nearby peasants into temporary armoured fighters for 45 seconds -- a panic button to survive an early rush. Send them back to mining after.
